h1: Product Photo Lighting for Glass, Metal, and Glossy Finishes
lead: Product photo lighting usually takes a lighting kit. Upload a plain snapshot and get a square photo with soft, directional light, gentle shadows, and the glow on glass and gold.
secondary_keywords: skincare product photo with soft light
intro: Glass, metal, and glossy packaging are hard to shoot at home, where a window throws glare in one spot and murky shadow in another. In the example, a square perfume bottle with a faceted cap glows with pale gold liquid, its collar catches a highlight, and soft shadows fall across a marble top scattered with white blossoms.

Controlled light can make glass edges and metal contours easier to see. Compare the result with your actual product before publishing. This approach suits perfume, serums, candles, watches, and other reflective items, including an extra Amazon image or a photo for your own store.
tip: Photograph your product against a plain wall with no direct sun on it, so harsh glare from the original doesn't carry into the new image.

faq.q: Which products work well with relighting?
faq.a: Glass, metal, ceramic, and glossy items can show useful changes in highlight and shadow.

faq.q: Can I describe a warmer or cooler look?
faq.a: Name the light color and direction, then keep the product shape and material visible.

faq.q: Do I need a studio setup?
faq.a: No. Start with a clear phone photo and describe the lighting look you want to try.

faq.q: Can I fix glare on glass or metal?
faq.a: Describe softer or warmer light and the generated photo keeps the same product with controlled highlights.

faq.q: Do I need real studio lights?
faq.a: No. The lighting is generated; a clear product photo and a written direction are enough.

faq.q: What does a relit photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits, shown before you run the job.

faq.q: Which light direction should I describe?
faq.a: Describe the direction that reveals the surface you need shoppers to see: soft window light from the left for a bottle edge, a broad front fill for a label, or a narrow side highlight for brushed metal. Name the shadow direction too so the result stays believable.

faq.q: Will relighting change my product shape or color?
faq.a: The brief asks the image to keep the uploaded product, but generated highlights can still shift a reflective surface. Compare the result with the real item, especially around caps, glass edges, and metallic finishes, and use your source photo for any detail that must be exact. If a reflection hides a label, move the light in the brief rather than asking for extra decoration. The goal is a controlled highlight that leaves the product identity and finish easy to compare.

faq.q: How do I reduce glare on glass or glossy plastic?
faq.a: Ask for broad side light, a soft front fill, and a controlled reflection that leaves the label and rim visible. Check the result at full size because a bright hotspot can still hide a curved edge.

faq.q: Can I choose the exact direction of the light?
faq.a: Yes. Name left, right, front, or back light and state where the shadow should fall. A direction plus a visible edge or label gives the generator a concrete lighting target.

faq.q: Which lighting scene belongs in an Amazon listing?
faq.a: Use even front fill and a readable product face for a listing image, then reserve macro or orbit highlights for ads and detail pages. Keep the approved source photo for any finish or color detail that must be exact.

overview.h2: Shape the Reflection Instead of Fighting It
overview.p: Glossy packaging can look premium in one light and unreadable in another. This template lets you explore a controlled direction—soft side light, an even studio wash, or a warmer tabletop mood—while keeping the product at the center of the frame.

A useful brief names the direction, softness, surface, and shadow before it names the mood. That gives you a repeatable starting point for a perfume bottle, serum jar, watch, candle, or cookware item.

visual.overview: Relighting helps a seller make reflective products easier to inspect without renting a studio. Upload a clear source photo, describe the direction and softness of the light, and use the square result for a [clean product listing photo](/ai-image-generation/ecommerce-main-image), an [Amazon product photo](/platforms/amazon-product-photos), or a [beauty product campaign](/industries/beauty-skincare). Compare the generated highlight with the real bottle, cap, glass edge, and metal finish before publishing; the source photo remains the reference for color and shape. Keep one lighting change in each version so a buyer can tell what improved. A soft highlight may reveal the curve of a bottle, while a darker edge can separate clear glass from a pale background.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. An adult turns the product once beside a bright window so its material catches a soft highlight. Natural light, clean UGC look. Close handheld shot with one small arc. Sound: quiet room tone, no music. End on the highlight.

picker.title: Choose a lighting ad scene
picker.lead: Choose a lighting scene by the surface you need shoppers to inspect: a soft highlight on glass, a controlled reflection on metal, or a clean finish on glossy packaging. Each example keeps the product central and uses one readable light change instead of adding a new prop story. The card prompts are useful when you need a repeatable brief for a collection: state the product material first, then the direction, softness, and surface. If the source has a blown-out reflection or a hidden edge, take a better source photo before asking for another light treatment. Treat the result as a merchandising image, not a color-calibration proof. Keep an unedited source image for any detail the generated light cannot prove, and compare reflective edges before publishing a listing image.
